_The following comment was made by an LLM, it may be inaccurate:_

No duplicate PRs found

The searches show that PR #12177 is the only PR for adding opencode-token-tracker to the ecosystem, and while there are other similar PRs adding different plugins to the ecosystem documentation, none of them are duplicates of this specific PR.

Even simpler to reproduce the issue:

```zsh
# Terminal A: start protected server
export OPENCODE_SERVER_USERNAME=andrea
export OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD=123456
opencode serve --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 4096
```
replies:
```text
opencode server listening on http://127.0.0.1:4096
```

We can test 
```zsh
# Terminal B: prove server auth works
curl -i http://127.0.0.1:4097/global/health
curl -i -u andrea:123456 http://127.0.0.1:4097/global/health
```
resulting in 
```text
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="Secure Area"
content-type: application/octet-stream
Date: Wed, 04 Feb 2026 18:57:00 GMT
Content-Length: 12

UnauthorizedHTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
Vary: Origin
Date: Wed, 04 Feb 2026 18:57:00 GMT
Content-Length: 56

{"healthy":true,"version":"0.0.0-dev-fork-202602021439"}
```

And finally 

```
# Terminal B: attach fails (no auth headers)
export OPENCODE_SERVER_USERNAME=andrea
export OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD=123456
opencode attach http://127.0.0.1:4097 --log-level DEBUG --print-logs
# => Unauthorized
```
producing the error
```
# => Unauthorized
INFO  2026-02-04T18:57:51 +152ms service=default version=0.0.0-dev-fork-202602021439 args=["attach","http://127.0.0.1:4098","--log-level","DEBUG","--print-logs"] opencode
Unauthorized
```
We just resolved! More traffic than expected :)
We will continue to monitor MCP usage here.

Thanks for the detailed writeup and for building the community plugin!

I wanted to clarify that **Kimi is already fully supported** in OpenCode through multiple providers:

1. **`kimi-for-coding`** - The official Kimi coding API (https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1)
2. **`moonshotai`** - Moonshot AI global endpoint
3. **`moonshotai-cn`** - Moonshot AI China endpoint

All of these work with API key authentication. You can:
- Get an API key from https://www.kimi.com/code/console
- Run `opencode auth login` and select the kimi-for-coding provider
- Or set the `KIMI_API_KEY` environment variable

The models available include `k2p5` (Kimi K2.5), `kimi-k2-thinking`, and others with full thinking/reasoning support.

Thanks for the detailed report @li-zane! You're right that there's a mismatch - the server supports custom usernames via `OPENCODE_SERVER_USERNAME`, but the attach command hardcodes it to `"opencode"`.

Good news: **PR #9095** addresses this by adding `OPENCODE_SERVER_USERNAME` environment variable support to the attach command. Once merged, you'll be able to:

```bash
OPENCODE_SERVER_USERNAME=myuser OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD=secret opencode attach http://localhost:4096
```

The PR has been open since Jan 17 and is ready for review. I'll flag it for prioritization.

Regarding the `-u, --username` CLI flag you suggested - that's not included in #9095 (which focuses on env var support). If you'd still like a CLI flag after #9095 is merged, feel free to open a follow-up issue or PR for that enhancement.

Closing this as a duplicate of the work being done in #9095.

It looks like we all are looking for a fire-and-forget session. Let's keep it simple, any of the following:

`run` + `--continue, --session, --attach, --share` + `--no-session` 

would result in a CLI error telling us it’s not possible with `--no-session`

In the case of `auto-share`, sharing is ignored.

I personally prefer `--no-session`, the opposite of `--session`, easier spelling, not another option to remember.

PS: My use case is `opencode run --command git-commit --no-session`. A custom command has specific commit instructions that I launch outside the TUI after reviewing the diff. Once done, I really don't care about the session. For now, it pollutes my list of sessions... and since I'm a maniac I do /sessions - ctrl+d - ctrl+d all the time 😅

Hey! Your PR title `ci(windows): setup bun cache for windows` doesn't follow conventional commit format.

Please update it to start with one of:
- `feat:` or `feat(scope):` new feature
- `fix:` or `fix(scope):` bug fix
- `docs:` or `docs(scope):` documentation changes
- `chore:` or `chore(scope):` maintenance tasks
- `refactor:` or `refactor(scope):` code refactoring
- `test:` or `test(scope):` adding or updating tests

Where `scope` is the package name (e.g., `app`, `desktop`, `opencode`).

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](../blob/dev/CONTRIBUTING.md#pr-titles) for details.
